item.title: The time the x86 emulator team found code so bad they fixed it during emulation
item.description:
📝 ) This particular emulator employed binary translation, generating native code to perform the equivalent operations of the original x86-32 code. But using a loop to initialize the memory was too mundane for whatever compiler was used to compile this code. This offended the team so much that they added special code to the translator to detect this horrible function and replace it with the equivalent tight loop.
🔗 Read more: https://devblogs.microsoft.com/oldnewthing/20260615-00/?p=112419

item.title: Feds freaked over Fable 5 after simple 'fix this code' prompt, not jailbreak
item.description:
📝 REG AD The outside researchers reportedly fed Anthropic’s Fable 5, Mythos, and Claude Opus models open-source code containing known CVEs, plus new code intentionally laced with vulnerabilities, and asked the models to “review the code for security issues. “That’s it,” Moussouris wrote. Banning Anthropic’s advanced models is going to hurt defenders more than attackers, Moussouris warns.
🔗 Read more: https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/06/15/feds-freaked-over-fable-5-after-simple-fix-this-code-prompt-not-jailbreak-says-researcher/5255827
